author: paulna
body:
Application
Age: 16
Timezone: Central Time Zone (UTC-6:00)
Do you have access to TeamSpeak? Yes/No: Yes
Do you have access to Skype? Yes/No: Yes
Do you have access to a recording software? Yes/No: Yes 

CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION

Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?
Yes, I was a helper on a small prison server known as "Quantum-Prison" but it has recently shut down. I'm aware of the certain criteria a staff member needs to follow and the example we as staff need to set in order to be respected by the community.

What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?
My biggest weakness, easy annoyance. Although this has never affected my position as staff member before, it sure is something I have a hard time dealing with. I easily get annoyed / stressed at things which makes it harder to take on a huge amount of something before starting to feel a bit stressed/annoyed.
My biggest strength, communication. I am a good speaker and enjoy talking with others, this can benefit my position as I can easily connect with the community easily without there being any type of  awkwardness.

How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?
I am always available. This can benefit the team by improving the "in-activeness" there is due to time zones, school, jobs etc. I am currently home-schooled which gives me liberty to be online moderating while working on homework etc. I've noticed there has been posts regarding "staff being inactive" so me being some sort of help may improve that small problem.

What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?
An open mind, integrity, and good communication. I consider myself to be a leader because at any given time, if there is a problem I can take care of I make sure to do so without hesitation. These three qualities I listed are things a leader needs, they need to be open to peoples opinions as well as respecting them, and of course there can't be a leader without some type of leading, so communication is a key factor here.

What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
My ability to comprehend. I am never quick to judge or make a decision without having second thoughts and facts to back me up. I can always be available, which means if there's any problem online, I'm most likely to be able to help.

What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?
Communication skills are a big factor in being a staff member, especially when interacting with the community. Without communication, both sides would be lost and have no idea what the problem / solution could be. These skills are great for helping a member with a problem, or dealing with an issue that affects plenty of people.

How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 
I can commit to 4-5 hours, more if needed.

CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?
If access to freeze, which I believe jr mods have, I'd freeze the person and contact higher authority. If the player continues to log off and come back with an alt, then I'll continue to repeat the process until a mod, sr mod, admin, etc. are available to ban them. Here, it would be a great idea for me to record everything so I can have solid evidence of the player logging off and coming back with a different account, in case the player decides to appeal.

Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?
Warn them, let them know that this isn't a way a staff member should be acting towards the community, if this was my first time dealing with this I would look at the rules regarding teamspeak and how to deal with the situation, if there's none I would contact a higher staff member to help me with the situation. Even though the person harassing people is a staff member, they should be following the rules like everybody else, to set an example.

A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realize that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?
If this were me, I would always upload the evidence to a private YouTube channel where I could have it handy if needed, for situations like these. But if there was no backup to this file corruption, I'd let the player know that he was seen hacking, and there were various other people around to back up my statement. If possible I would ask any of the other players if they recorded it so I could use that to provide evidence.

You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?
Inform a higher staff, even if not that important, there should be knowledge of the situation so that the player doesn't leak more important stuff knowing he wasn't punished for his first offence.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?
Although not 100% confirmed, I would respect the senior staff and their decision. I would not do anything about it unless the information I was told was 100% true or it came from the staff member themselves.

CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?
It would be a great step for me, being a long time member of this community truly has had it's rewards. Getting moderator would mean being able to help the community more, to be able to do something about the hackers, etc. This would give me the benefit of being taken seriously by the community. I am apart of this servers community and don't plan to go anywhere any time soon, being a moderator would just plain out be a great accomplishment to my dedication to this server, and love for helping.

How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?
Very passionate, I play on the server and check the forums regularly. Avicus is like a family to me, the community here is just so kind and funny, the staff team is dedicated and are always helpful. Overall Avicus is somewhere I feel I can be myself without fearing hate.

Do you speak any other languages than English?
Yes, I speak some-what fluent Spanish.

Do you have anything else to add to your application?
My other account is gxc, I believe this is something I should add. Thank you to the staff team for reading my application. :)
